_metadata.source: NASA Exoplanet Archive (Planetary Systems Composite Parameters table)
_metadata.description: Curated selection of publicly verified exoplanet observations for BioSphere-X scientific expedition modeling. Uses only authentic published fields, preserves original source units, and documents scientific constraints.
scientific_caveats: Theoretical Equilibrium Temperature (pl_eqt) is a calculated blackbody temperature assuming an idealized Bond albedo; it does NOT represent confirmed surface temperature, which requires atmospheric modeling and greenhouse gas analysis.
Planet radius alone is insufficient to calculate surface gravity; true surface gravity strictly requires a confirmed mass measurement from radial velocity or transit timing variations (TTV).
Orbital eccentricity (pl_orbeccen) quantifies orbital ellipse elongation and annual stellar flux variations; it is NOT a direct measurement of diurnal day/night cycle or rotation period.

exoplanets.notes: Earth-sized planet in the habitable zone of an ultra-cool red dwarf. High bulk density indicates rocky composition.
First validated Earth-sized planet in habitable zone. Mass unmeasured by radial velocity or TTV; surface gravity remains unconfirmed.
Closest known exoplanet to Earth. Detected via Doppler radial velocity; non-transiting so geometric radius is unmeasured.
Discovered by TESS. Earth-sized candidate receiving 86% of Earth's solar insolation. Mass currently unmeasured.
Super-Earth with high-precision transit and Doppler radial velocity measurements. Dense rocky interior.
Sub-Neptune / Hycean candidate with detected atmospheric water vapor absorption. Significant orbital eccentricity.
Extreme ultra-hot Jupiter orbiting an F-type star in approximately 1.1 days. Subject to extreme stellar tidal forces and hyperthermal radiation.
